lines.text: Why do we light so many lamps? the child asks.
Because a whole city once waited for someone to come home.
In North India, Diwali remembers Rama's return to Ayodhya
with Sita and Lakshmana, after fourteen years of exile and his victory over Ravana.
On the darkest night of Kartik, the people cleaned their homes,
lit a diya at every door, and the road home became a river of light.
That is the heart of Diwali: light over darkness, good over evil,
and a home that keeps a lamp burning.
The festival is five days: Dhanteras, Chhoti Diwali, Lakshmi Puja,
Govardhan Puja, and Bhai Dooj, the bond of brothers and sisters.
Homes are cleaned, rangoli drawn at the door, sweets shared,
and Lakshmi welcomed with lamps and a prayer for prosperity and peace.
In the north, grain and cattle are honoured on Govardhan;
brothers and sisters mark Bhai Dooj with a tilak and a shared meal.
So the diya is not only a lamp.
It is a city remembering, a family giving, and a promise that light returns to every home.

cues.note: a low drum under the waiting city

silences.why: the breath before the dark field
the last flame holds before the door
the tail fade is the ending

motifs.meaning: the light that is passed from hand to hand
the mark of the bond between siblings
the threshold where the welcome is made

visual.shows: a low doorway at night, one clay diya on the step, a child standing beside it
visual.action: the child stands at the clay diya and leans into the flame; the doorway glows
visual.focus: the small flame and the child's lit face
visual.why: the question is asked beside the first lamp, so the answer starts at a doorstep

performers.does: stands at the clay diya and leans into the flame
performers.why: the question is the child's, and the film answers it at the child's eye level

direction.entry: a low doorway, one diya, a child at the step
direction.exit: the flame steadies and the child settles beside it
direction.spine: the film begins with the question and the smallest lamp

events.note: the first flame answers the child's question
the child watches the first flame
the child looks into the light
the child's hand moves toward the flame
the child reaches toward the flame

visual.shows: a wide moon over Ayodhya, empty rooftops and one lit lamp below
visual.action: the city holds still and the lamp does not move
visual.focus: the single lamp under the moon
visual.why: the line says a whole city waited, so the frame is the city before anyone arrives

direction.entry: a moon over a sleeping city
direction.exit: the rooftops hold and the lamp keeps its flame
direction.spine: the city is the thing that waits

events.note: a shutter shifts in the wind

visual.shows: three travellers before the city gate of Ayodhya, a river and roofs behind
visual.action: Rama leads Sita and Lakshmana toward the gate
visual.focus: the tallest traveller and the open gate
visual.why: the line names the return, so the frame is the road into the city that waited

direction.entry: a gate, a river and three small travellers
direction.exit: the travellers reach the gate and a lamp appears beyond it
direction.spine: the city and the road are the same welcome

events.note: a lamp appears beyond the gate

visual.shows: three silhouettes on a forest path, Sita's silhouette between Rama and Lakshmana
visual.action: the three walk between torn trunks
visual.why: the line names who went into exile, so the frame counts the three bodies on the path

direction.entry: a dark forest path with three walkers
direction.exit: the three pass between the trunks
direction.spine: exile is walked by three people, not one

events.note: the middle figure steps over a root
a leaf lets the moon through

visual.shows: Rama under a gold sun, the broken bow of Ravana at his feet
visual.action: Rama lifts his crown as the broken bow falls
visual.focus: the broken bow on the ground
visual.why: the line names the victory, so the frame shows the weapon that ended the exile

direction.entry: a gold sun and a crowned figure
direction.exit: the bow lies broken and the crown catches the light
direction.spine: the exile ends with a broken bow

visual.shows: one lit diya in a black field under Kartik stars
visual.action: the wick catches and the flame grows
visual.why: the line names the darkest night, so the frame is one flame with nothing else around it

direction.entry: a black field and a single clay lamp
direction.exit: the flame stands alone under the stars
direction.spine: the night is dark enough that one flame is the picture

visual.shows: five doorways along a night street, a diya at every doorstep
visual.action: the flames catch from door to door
visual.why: the line counts the doors, so the frame is a street where each threshold has its own lamp

direction.entry: a street of doorways, the first lamp just lit
direction.spine: the welcome is repeated at every threshold

events.note: the street warms to the end

visual.shows: a road of lamps running to the city gate, light opening the dark
visual.action: the lamps flow toward the gate and the dark recedes
visual.why: the line says light over darkness, so the frame is a road made only of flames

direction.entry: a dark road with one flame
direction.exit: the road reaches the gate in light
direction.spine: the road is the argument: light wins by repeating

events.note: the gate lifts out of the dark

visual.phrase: a home that keeps a lamp
visual.shows: a house with one lit window and a diya on the sill
visual.action: the window glow steadies as the lamp burns
visual.why: the line names the home, so the frame is one house with one lamp still awake

direction.entry: a dark house with one window awake
direction.spine: a home is a lamp that has not gone out

visual.shows: five tall paper panels hanging on a cream wall, each with an unlit lamp
visual.action: the five panels drop into a row and their lamps catch
visual.why: the line counts the festival, so the frame counts five panels before it names them

direction.entry: a bare cream wall and five lamps
direction.exit: five panels stand in a row, every lamp lit
direction.spine: the festival is counted before it is named

visual.shows: three paper name cards for Dhanteras, Chhoti Diwali and Lakshmi Puja on a cream wall
visual.action: each card turns to face the row of five panels
visual.why: the line names three of the days, so the frame names the same three in order

direction.entry: a cream wall with three blank cards
direction.exit: three cards face the five lit panels
direction.spine: the first three days are named before the last two

visual.shows: five panels on the wall, the last two lit, a tilak card below Govardhan Puja and Bhai Dooj
visual.action: the last two lamps catch and the tilak card is stamped
visual.why: the line finishes the five names, so the frame lights only the panels it has just named

direction.entry: five panels, the first three waiting
direction.exit: the last two panels light and the tilak card holds
direction.spine: the last two days finish the row

visual.shows: a rangoli blooming on a cream floor, a child placing a marigold at its rim
visual.action: the child places a marigold at the rangoli rim and the powder lines settle
visual.focus: the flower at the rangoli rim
visual.why: the line names the rangoli at the door, so the frame is the drawing and the hand that finishes it

performers.does: places a marigold at the rangoli rim
performers.why: the welcome at the door is made by the child's hand

direction.entry: a rangoli half drawn on the floor
direction.exit: the flower sits at the rim and the powder holds
direction.spine: the welcome is drawn before it is spoken

events.note: the child sets it at the rim
a lamp beyond the rangoli warms the floor

visual.shows: Lakshmi in a red shrine, a brass thali of lamps and marigold before her
visual.action: the thali is lifted and the lamps lean toward the shrine
visual.why: the line welcomes Lakshmi, so the frame is the offering carried to her

direction.entry: a red shrine and a covered thali
direction.exit: the thali is raised and the lamps lean
direction.spine: the goddess is welcomed with what the house can carry

visual.shows: a green hill, a cow and a grain bundle tied with red thread
visual.action: the grain bundle is lifted and the cow bows its head
visual.focus: the red thread on the grain
visual.why: the line names grain and cattle, so the frame carries both at the edge of the field

direction.entry: a green field, a hill, a cow and a grain bundle
direction.exit: the grain is raised and the cow bows
direction.spine: the field and the animal are thanked together

visual.phrase: a tilak and a shared meal
visual.shows: a sister marking a tilak on her brother's forehead, a sweet for the shared meal on the step
visual.action: the sister presses the tilak on the brother's forehead and the brother offers a sweet for the shared meal
visual.why: the line names the tilak and the meal, so the frame is the mark and the sweet exchanged at the door

performers.does: presses the tilak on the brother's forehead
performers.why: the line names the tilak, and the elder sibling makes the mark

performers.does: offers a sweet for the shared meal
performers.why: the line names the shared meal, and the younger sibling gives the sweet

direction.entry: two siblings at a lit door
direction.exit: the tilak is set and the sweet passes between them
direction.spine: the bond is performed as a mark and a gift

events.note: the elder raises a hand to the forehead

visual.phrase: the diya is not only a lamp
visual.shows: one great diya in the foreground, a row of smaller flames behind it
visual.action: the great flame steadies and the row answers
visual.why: the line turns the lamp into a promise, so the frame shows one flame and the many it stands for

direction.entry: one great diya and a dark row behind
direction.exit: the row answers the great flame
direction.spine: one lamp is a promise because it is repeated

visual.shows: a match touching a fresh wick, a row of family lamps behind
visual.action: the match touches the wick and the fresh flame catches
visual.why: the line names the family giving, so the frame is the flame handed to the next lamp

direction.entry: a match above a fresh diya
direction.spine: the giving is a small physical act

events.note: the wick leans into the heat

visual.shows: the child stands before a long row of flames on the step
visual.action: the child watches the row and the light returns along the step
visual.why: the promise is kept by the child standing with the row, not by another match

performers.does: watches the row so the light returns to the doorway
performers.why: the child is the next keeper of the light, and the row answers the child

direction.entry: a row of flames and a child at the end of it
direction.exit: the child holds the new flame up and the row answers
direction.spine: the child is the next keeper of the light

events.note: the child lifts the new diya
the child watches the row answer
the child holds the diya higher
